title: Manufacturable ultra-low-voltage switching for general-purpose electronics

concept.text: The innovation would be a manufacturable electronic switch that enables dense, reliable general-purpose logic to operate at substantially lower supply voltage while retaining useful performance. Its success would depend on combining low switching energy with adequate on-current, low off-state leakage, speed, endurance and consistent behavior across large numbers of devices. The intended capability extends from individual transistors through integrated processors and their supporting systems.

A central device property is subthreshold swing, the gate-voltage change needed to change current by a factor of ten in the switching region. A smaller value can help a transistor move between its off and on states over a smaller voltage interval, providing a route toward lower-voltage logic. The supplied papers explore hot-emitter transistors and threshold-switch-integrated vertical transistors as approaches to steep switching. Translating their measured switching behavior into practical low-voltage circuits remains part of the innovation.

significance.text: Reliable switching at substantially reduced supply voltage could lower the energy consumed by logic operations. If this capability survived dense integration and delivered a large reduction in energy per useful computation at comparable throughput and reliability, its reach across general-purpose electronics could make it revolutionary. The supplied vertical-transistor paper explicitly connects reduced subthreshold swing with the possibility of lowering supply voltage and transistor power consumption.

As a conditional system-level synthesis, a sufficiently large energy advantage could reduce computing power requirements, heat generation and operating costs. It could also extend the useful computation available within fixed battery, cooling or facility-power budgets. Those downstream possibilities depend on how much total energy the new switching technology actually saves, together with its performance, reliability and manufacturing economics. Lower manufacturing cost would require separate evidence.

The impact must be assessed across the whole computing system. Memory, interconnects, leakage, power delivery and cooling contribute energy costs that may limit the benefit of improved logic switching. A very small measured subthreshold swing establishes a particular device characteristic. The revolutionary outcome would additionally require a measured advantage in useful computation under practical operating conditions. This whole-system interpretation is a synthesis of the general-purpose goal.

missing_breakthrough.text: The missing capability is the simultaneous achievement of steep switching and practical electrical performance in a reproducible fabrication process. Liu and colleagues identify the need to reduce off-current, increase on-current and improve the on-to-off current ratio. Their reported hot-emitter devices also retain leakage, hysteresis and a limited current range over which steep switching occurs. These constraints make the usable switching window and device behavior across operating conditions central engineering questions.

Scaling a promising device into reliable logic requires control of device variation, fabrication quality, switching speed and endurance. Yang and colleagues address scaling and report limited cycling tests, providing evidence relevant to this transition. Their device-level results leave substantial work in demonstrating production consistency and operating lifetime for integrated computing.

As an engineering synthesis of the proposed general-purpose capability, dense circuits must preserve adequate voltage margins, usable signal levels and predictable operation while incorporating memory and interconnects. Lower supply voltage must remain compatible with the current needed to drive circuit loads and with reliable operation across device variation and operating conditions. Manufacturing yield, integration compatibility and lifetime qualification would have to support the same system that delivers the energy advantage.

current_state.text: On 14 August 2024, Chi Liu and colleagues published a room-temperature hot-emitter transistor demonstration. The reported minimum subthreshold swing ranged from 0.38 to 1.52 mV per decade depending on bias, supporting a below-1 mV per decade minimum under some reported conditions. Sub-60 mV per decade switching extended over approximately one to three decades of current. Substantial leakage and hysteresis remained among the practical limitations.

Liu and colleagues also described a three-device hot-emitter logic example operated with multi-volt biases. This adds a circuit demonstration to the device results, while leaving the proposed ultra-low-supply-voltage processor capability unestablished. The minimum slope, the current range over which it occurs and the voltages required by a working circuit are separate measures of progress.

On 7 February 2024, Qiyu Yang and colleagues published threshold-switch-integrated vertical transistors built from sub-5 nm thin van der Waals heterostructures. They reported a current modulation ratio exceeding 100 million and average subthreshold swing below 60 mV per decade over six decades of drain current during forward gate sweeps. Performance calculations used a 30 fA measurement floor. The sweep direction and treatment of the detection limit therefore matter when interpreting the reported range and metrics, and currents below that floor were not independently validated in the supplied review.

Yang and colleagues reported no performance degradation after 1,000 on-off switching cycles in drain-source and gate-voltage cycling tests. This provides a bounded endurance demonstration. Establishing processor lifetime would require substantially broader qualification. The authors describe the technology as a proof of concept for ultra-scaled, low-power digital logic, and the supplied demonstrations leave manufacturable general-purpose processors with a transformative system-level energy advantage to be demonstrated.

The supplied review had full article text for both papers, including methods and extended-data captions for Liu's article. Figures were not visually inspected, and Yang's supplementary information was unavailable for independent inspection. These limits constrain evaluation of graphical evidence and supplementary tests while preserving the attributed findings supported by the reviewed article text.

The supplied record establishes dated demonstrations from 2024. Its freshness record contains no bounded search entries, so the field's status as of 1 November 2026 remains unresolved. The evidence supplied here cannot determine whether later work has closed the remaining gaps. It also provides no basis for calling a sub-5 mV per decade slope a historical or universal completion target.

completion_criteria.text: A proposed convincing demonstration would fabricate reproducible integrated processors using the switching technology and independently compare representative workloads with leading conventional systems at comparable throughput and reliability. The evaluation should specify workload selection, baseline systems, operating conditions and system boundaries before testing. These are proposed criteria for evaluating this innovation.
completion_criteria.label: Reproducible processors independently benchmarked at comparable throughput and reliability

completion_criteria.text: The proposed comparison should demonstrate a predefined, substantial reduction in whole-system energy per useful computation, accounting for memory, interconnects, power delivery and cooling. Energy measurements should include all supplies and supporting components required by the implementation within the declared boundary. The required magnitude of improvement remains to be specified.
completion_criteria.label: Predefined substantial whole-system energy reduction per useful computation

completion_criteria.text: A proposed reproducibility and practicality assessment would examine device distributions across fabrication batches, circuit yield, operating voltage margins, leakage, speed, endurance and lifetime. It would require a credible manufacturing path and independently reproducible operation within declared temperature, workload and reliability boundaries. Quantitative acceptance thresholds should be established before testing, with disclosure of failure rates and operating exclusions.
completion_criteria.label: Credible manufacturing path and independently reproducible operation within declared boundaries

completion_criteria.text: A switching-slope measurement would contribute device evidence to this assessment, alongside measured current range, bias conditions and usable circuit performance. No universal sub-5 mV per decade requirement is proposed. Finite workload and operating-condition tests would establish demonstrated breadth within their stated boundaries. Claims of broader general-purpose applicability would remain proportionate to that evidence.
completion_criteria.label: Measured switching slope and circuit performance bound general-purpose claims

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis links ELE-08 closely with ELE-04, Practical, energy-recovering reversible computing. Both seek lower computation energy. ELE-08 focuses on manufacturable low-voltage switches and their integration into general-purpose electronics, while ELE-04 centers on reversible operation and energy recovery. Their benefits could potentially be combined, subject to compatible device and circuit requirements.

ELE-11, Integrated photonic-electronic computing with broad system advantage, shares the requirement to translate component improvements into useful whole-system gains. Photonic-electronic integration concerns the division and integration of optical and electronic functions. ELE-08 concerns electronic switching, which could also support electronic portions of such systems. ELE-02, Fault-tolerant quantum computer with useful, scalable logical computation, and ELE-03, A long-distance quantum repeater network, pursue quantum capabilities with distinct completion requirements. More efficient supporting electronics could complement those efforts.

ELE-10, Broadly deployable, maintenance-free ambient-powered sensing, could benefit from reduced electronic energy requirements, while still requiring sufficient harvested energy and reliable sensing operation. ELE-06, Durable, high-bandwidth two-way neural interface, could similarly benefit from lower-power electronics, alongside its separate biological, interface and durability requirements. These are conditional application connections inferred from the roster.

ELE-01, Practical ambient-temperature superconducting conductors, concerns conductor performance and could complement low-energy electronic systems through suitable supporting infrastructure. ELE-05, Cheap, scalable storage for weeks to seasons of electrical supply, ELE-07, Infrastructure-scale wireless electrical power delivery, and ELE-09, Resilient, self-restoring power networks, address storage, delivery and grid operation. Reduced computing demand could affect the loads those systems serve. Each retains a separate technological objective and demonstration burden.

change_log.change: Preserved ELE-08 and its title, and developed the concept from a switching-slope claim into the intended manufacturable, integrated general-purpose capability.
change_log.reason: The candidate and review define success through practical performance, reliability and energy per useful computation.

change_log.change: Specified Liu's bias-dependent minimum swing range, approximately one-to-three-decade steep-switching range, leakage, hysteresis and multi-volt three-device logic example.
change_log.reason: These reviewed details distinguish an exceptional device measurement from demonstrated ultra-low-voltage circuit operation.

change_log.change: Added Yang's publication date, heterostructure scale, current modulation ratio, forward-sweep scope, 30 fA measurement floor and 1,000-cycle endurance result.
change_log.reason: The quantitative results require their measurement and qualification boundaries to remain interpretable.

change_log.change: Removed the characterization of sub-5 mV per decade as a historical target and retained the conclusion that slope alone cannot establish completion.
change_log.reason: The supplied sources do not establish that historical target, and the proposed capability requires integrated-system evidence.

change_log.change: Expanded completion proposals to include interconnects, predefined evaluation boundaries, baseline selection, energy thresholds and reliability qualification.
change_log.reason: These additions make the proposed assessment operational while preserving its status as a proposal.

change_log.change: Integrated conditional downstream benefits, whole-system limits and the distinction between operating costs and manufacturing economics.
change_log.reason: Device-level power motivation supports conditional impact reasoning, while broader economic outcomes require additional evidence.

change_log.change: Preserved review access limitations and unresolved freshness, and labeled roster relationships and unsourced evaluation proposals as synthesis.
change_log.reason: The record must distinguish supplied evidence from inference and avoid implying additional document inspection or research.

unresolved_issues: The field's status as of 1 November 2026 remains unresolved because the supplied freshness record contains no bounded search entries.
The magnitude of the required whole-system energy advantage and quantitative manufacturing, reliability and lifetime acceptance thresholds remain unspecified.
Yang's supplementary information was unavailable to the supplied review, and neither paper's figures were visually inspected.
Interpretation of Yang's performance metrics remains bounded by the disclosed 30 fA measurement floor and forward-sweep conditions.
The supplied evidence does not establish a historical sub-5 mV per decade target.
The supplied record does not establish independent replication, production-scale uniformity or processor-level validation of the reported device approaches.

brief.title: Computer switches that need much less voltage
possible: People could use computers that do the same useful work with much less electricity. This would require tiny electronic switches that work reliably at much lower voltage and can be manufactured consistently in dense chips.
Battery-powered devices could do more computing between charges. Computers could also do more work within the power and cooling limits of a building.
why: Lower energy use could mean less heat and lower operating costs for people and organisations running computers. The benefit would come from reducing the electricity needed for useful computation across the whole machine.

sources.showed: They built a transistor, an electronic switch, whose current changed sharply with a small voltage change at room temperature. They also demonstrated a small logic circuit.
sources.quote: Multi-valued logic with a high inverter gain and reconfigurable logic states are further demonstrated.
sources.cited_for: Sharp switching and a small logic circuit demonstrate parts of the route toward lower-voltage computing.
sources.not_established: The circuit still needed multi-volt supplies, and the switches retained unwanted current flow while off and dependence on previous voltages.

sources.showed: They built transistors with current flowing vertically through thin stacked layers. The devices combined sharp switching with a large difference between on and off current.
sources.quote:
an excellent current modulation ratio
exceeding 1 × 108 at room temperature.
sources.cited_for: Thin vertical devices can combine sharp switching with a large separation between on and off current.
sources.not_established: Device tests did not establish manufacturing consistency, processor lifetime or energy savings in a working computer.

shown: Chi Liu and colleagues demonstrated sharp switching at room temperature and a small logic circuit. Qiyu Yang and colleagues combined sharp switching with a thin vertical design and reported no performance loss after 1,000 switching cycles.
missing: Switches still need to combine low voltage, enough current while on, little current while off, speed and long life.
Dense processors still need reliable signals and predictable operation despite differences between devices and operating conditions.
A repeatable manufacturing process still needs to deliver consistent devices and a high share of working circuits.
Working computers still need to demonstrate substantial energy savings at comparable speed and reliability, including their supporting components.

milestones.label: Repeatable processors match conventional speed and reliability
milestones.explanation: Independently tested processors would have to match leading conventional systems on representative tasks under comparison rules set beforehand. This would establish useful computing performance.

milestones.label: Whole computers use substantially less energy
milestones.explanation: Tests would have to meet an energy-saving target set beforehand, counting memory, connections, power delivery and cooling. This would establish savings per useful computation across the whole system.

milestones.label: Manufacturing and reliable operation prove repeatable
milestones.explanation: Fabrication batches and independent tests would have to meet preset limits for device variation, working circuits, speed and lifetime under stated conditions. This would establish a credible manufacturing path.

milestones.label: Switch measurements and circuit tests support computing claims
milestones.explanation: Tests would have to measure how much voltage changes current, over what current range, alongside circuit performance. This would tie claims of general-purpose use to demonstrated tasks and operating conditions.

uncertain: The required energy saving and acceptable manufacturing, reliability and lifetime limits remain unspecified.
The vertical devices' reported performance depends on the direction of voltage change and the instrument's lowest measurable current.
Independent replication and the breadth of reliable general-purpose operation remain open questions.
